marks.gloss_en: דאמר רבי אסי אמר רבי יוחנן: עשר נטיעות, ערבה וניסוך המים — הלכה למשה מסיני (no support kind for a דאמר citation; svara)
and the Rabbis -- whence the [willow] of the Temple? they have it as a received halakha
מאי קראה: קח על מים רבים צפצפה שמו -- R' Zeira's verse for the baraita's exclusion (no support kind for מאי קראה; svara)
'willows of the brook' -- those that grow by the brook
אמר רבי אבהו ... ומאי ניהו — ערבה, והן שמו עצמן כצפצפה שבהרים -- adduced for the reading Abaye attacked
אמר ליה אביי: ודילמא פרושי קא מפרש -- קח על מים רבים, ומאי ניהו? צפצפה! -- perhaps the verse is explaining: what was placed by many waters is the tzaftzafa
אם כן, מאי שמו? -- if so, what is 'he set it'? (unmarked, so the stam's; header) -- followed by R' Abbahu's homily (s_abbahu_v1)
R' Abbahu: the Holy One said: I said Israel should be before Me like 'taken by many waters' -- which is the willow -- and they set themselves as the tzaftzafa of the mountains
אמר רבי אבהו ... (the איכא דמתני tradition) -- adduced for the reading R' Zeira attacked
מתקיף לה רבי זירא: ודילמא פרושי קא מפרש -- קח על מים רבים, מאי ניהו? צפצפה! (the איכא דמתני tradition)
אם כן — מאי שמו? -- followed by R' Abbahu's homily (s_abbahu_v2)
some teach this verse as part of the baraita: 'he took it by many waters, he set it as a tzaftzafa'
שמע מינה -- from the baraita (sickle-edge fit) as he has just read it, the chilfa gila is fit (no support kind for an amora's שמע מינה; svara)
Abaye: conclude from it that this chilfa gila is fit for the hoshana
והא תניא: דומה למגל כשר, דומה למסר פסול! -- a sickle-like edge is fit, yet the baraita makes it the tzaftzafa's mark
כי תניא ההיא — בחילפא גילא (= p_abaye_chilfa_gila)
the willow: its stem is red, its leaf drawn out, and its edge smooth
ואימא הכי נמי! -- say it is indeed so: having a qualifying name, it is not fit (attacks the מהו דתימא of 34a.7; header)
ערבי נחל אמר רחמנא, מכל מקום (= p_stam_mikol_makom)
the Merciful One said 'willows of the brook' -- in any case
Abba Shaul: 'willows' -- two: one for the lulav and one for the Temple
Rav Chisda: these three things' names changed since the Temple was destroyed: chalafta -- aravta, aravta -- chalafta
Rav Chisda: shofara -- chatzotzrta, chatzotzrta -- shofara
Rav Chisda: petorta -- petora, petora -- petorta
Abaye: I too say: bei kasei -- huvlila, huvlila -- bei kasei
what practical difference does it make? for a needle found in the thickness of the beit hakosot
Rava bar Yosef: I too say: Bavel -- Bursif, Bursif -- Bavel
